## TL;DR

Addressed the two Pipeline regressions reported in review. A running agent that has crossed the existing silence threshold now resolves to Stuck even if process telemetry still says running, so Pipeline surfaces the same stuck signal as Board. Pipeline hides inline elapsed time only while work is actively in flight; idle review and close-out cards retain their state duration. The scoped RepoOS check passed after updating tooltip test fixtures to describe healthy in-flight work.

## Work and rationale

The review identified two related problems in the Pipeline presentation. First, `resolveSharedTaskCardStatus` checked the `running` signal before checking whether the task had exceeded its silence threshold. In that combination, the shared state became Coding and dropped the Stuck signal. Pipeline then hid elapsed time for the resulting healthy state, leaving no indication that the agent had gone quiet. I moved the existing threshold check ahead of the generic running fallback, after the higher-priority handoff/check and queue cases. This preserves live check and handoff status while allowing prolonged silence to supersede stale running telemetry. The existing shared resolver means Board and Pipeline now consume the same result.

Second, Pipeline previously hid elapsed time whenever `displayState` was `ok`. That condition also covered idle “In review” and close-out cards, including rows whose agent activity timestamp is absent. I changed the condition to hide elapsed only when shared status reports active in-flight work that is not stuck. Active coding and checks continue to place last-activity recency on their step tooltip, while idle rows keep their elapsed state time. Stuck rows also retain elapsed inline.

I added Pipeline coverage for a silent task with `running: true`, checking that it renders Stuck and elapsed time through the full PipelineView-to-PipelineCard path. Table-driven review and close-out cases verify that idle rows preserve elapsed time with no activity timestamp. The healthy tooltip, touch interaction, and check-progress fixtures now provide explicit live-work status signals. This makes the setup match the condition under test and keeps tooltip expectations meaningful after narrowing elapsed suppression. The Pipeline portion remains in the bundle because these fixes and regression cases share the same recency presentation and remain a small, coherent change.

## Approaches tried

I first traced the review findings through `PipelineView`, `PipelineCard`, and the shared status resolver. The Pipeline view already passes the silence duration and stuck signal, so duplicating status derivation inside Pipeline would have created inconsistent behavior. I kept the fix in the shared resolver and limited Pipeline’s elapsed rule to the `inFlight` status property. I then ran the required changed-path check. Its first attempt exposed two fixtures that depended on the previous broad `ok` behavior; I corrected those fixtures to model live healthy work and reran the full scoped gate.

## Challenges and blockers

The configured `thinkpad` remote runner hung twice during this session. RepoOS terminated the hung validation containers and retried automatically on `bee`. The first complete suite run finished with two tooltip tests failing because their Pipeline props did not indicate in-flight work. After updating those fixtures, the retry completed successfully. There are no outstanding implementation blockers.

## Key learnings

Pipeline state and elapsed time answer different questions: live work should emphasize what the agent is doing and expose activity recency on demand, while idle review and close-out rows need elapsed time even if no agent activity timestamp exists. A generic visual state such as `ok` is too broad to drive elapsed visibility; the shared lifecycle’s `inFlight` and `stuck` signals express the relevant distinction. Silence checks also need to account for stale process telemetry when elapsed activity has crossed the established threshold.

Verification: `REPOOS_CHECK_CHANGED=main repoos check` passed on the final implementation. The remote changed-path run passed build and 5,088 tests (one skipped), plus contrast and UI smoke checks. Local format, lint, build, CSS/theme checks, rendered contrast audit, and UI smoke checks also passed.
